rationale: Identity verification was handled correctly (name + zip matched to a single user). The agent sought confirmation before proceeding. However, several policy violations occurred: (1) The agent listed product variant options that were not supported by the tool results (e.g., keyboard variants and thermostat GA/black availability were not verified; some GA variants shown were unavailable). (2) It executed the exchange using item_ids and a payment_method_id that were not fetched or confirmed by tools, indicating fabricated details. (3) It asserted that the price difference would be refunded without confirming amounts or even whether a refund vs. charge was due. Tool feedback after the exchange didn’t clearly confirm success, yet the agent stated it was processed. These constitute acting on unsupported facts and performing writes with unverified details, failing the policy’s requirements to inspect with read-only tools and avoid fabrication.
